snp1.2:1.2: The name Dhaniya Gopa means roughly "the one whose wealth is cattle"; according to the commentary (SnA), his herd numbered 30,000 head.
snp1.2:2.1: The Buddha's opening line puns on Dhaniya's: "free from anger" (akkodhano) echoes Dhaniya's "rice is cooked" (pakkodano), and "rigidity" (khilo) echoes his "milk" (khīro).
snp1.2:2.4: "Open" describes a mind no longer covered by craving, defilement, or ignorance — the same image appears at Ud 5:5 and Sn 4:4. "My fire out" refers to the fires of passion, aversion, and delusion, and of birth, aging, and death, and of sorrow, lamentation, pain, distress, and despair; see SN 35:28, Iti 93, and The Mind Like Fire Unbound.
snp1.2:4.1: The raft is a figure for the noble eightfold path; see MN 22 and SN 35:197.
snp1.2:4.4: Since this verse doesn't read as a direct reply to the one before it, the commentary (SnA) suggests part of the exchange has been lost. Alternatively, the Buddha may be punning, since "crossed over" (tiṇṇa) echoes Dhaniya's word for grass (tiṇa).
snp1.2:8.1: Per the commentary, the Buddha is employed by no one — not even by himself — meaning he is not in the employ of craving.
snp1.2:10.4: This may be literal, since he owns no cattle and so heavy rain poses no threat through them, or it may be metaphorical; see SN 4:19 and Thag 1:1.
snp1.2:12.5: This verse is quoted in the Milindapañha.
snp1.2:14.3: On the epithet "One with Eyes" for the Buddha, see DN 16, note 44, and Sn 2:12, note 2.
snp1.2:16.2: According to the commentary, Māra appears here to try, unsuccessfully, to keep Dhaniya and his wife from going forth; this same exchange between Māra and the Buddha also appears at SN 4:8.
